title: Canada Issues 3,000 Invitations in Latest Canadian Experience Class Express Entry Draw
excerpt: IRCC held its 13th CEC draw of 2026 on August 5, maintaining a CRS cutoff of 516 as total invitations for the year surpass 108,000.
body:
• Canada issued 3,000 invitations to apply for permanent residence in a Canadian Experience Class Express Entry draw on August 5, with a CRS cutoff of 516
  • The draw brings total CEC invitations in 2026 to 48,250 across 13 rounds, making it the most active Express Entry pathway this year
  • CRS cutoff scores have held steady in the 514-518 range since March, reflecting consistent demand and stable pool sizes
  • IRCC has issued 108,123 total Express Entry invitations across all categories in 2026, with French-language draws accounting for 40,500

Latest Draw Details

Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) issued 3,000 invitations to apply for permanent residence on August 5 in a draw targeting Canadian Experience Class (CEC) candidates, according to CIC News.

https://x.com/Olufemiloye/status/2085017320020144204

Candidates needed a minimum Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS) score of 516 and must have created their Express Entry profile before 9:35 p.m. UTC on July 3, 2026. The cutoff score matches the two most recent CEC draws — held on July 21 and June 23 — signaling a stable competitive threshold.

A Busy Year for CEC Draws

The August 5 draw is the 13th CEC-specific round of 2026 and the 44th Express Entry draw overall this year. IRCC has now issued 48,250 invitations through the Canadian Experience Class alone, more than any other Express Entry pathway.

CRS cutoffs for CEC draws have remained remarkably consistent in 2026, ranging from 507 to 518 across all rounds. The stability suggests the pool of eligible candidates is being replenished at roughly the same rate as invitations are issued.

The draw sizes have varied more widely. Early 2026 CEC rounds saw larger draws of 6,000 to 8,000 invitations, while recent rounds have settled into a 2,000-3,000 range. The June 23 draw was an exception at 4,000 invitations — the largest CEC round since March.

Express Entry in 2026

Across all draw types, IRCC has issued 108,123 invitations through Express Entry in 2026. The breakdown by category:

Canadian Experience Class leads with 48,250 invitations across 13 draws. French-language proficiency draws account for 40,500 invitations, reflecting Ottawa's continued prioritization of francophone immigration. The Provincial Nominee Program has seen 15 draws totaling 6,957 invitations, while healthcare-focused rounds have issued 8,000 invitations.

Smaller category-based draws have targeted trade occupations (3,000), physicians with Canadian work experience (662), senior managers (750), and skilled military recruits (4).

"So far this year, the department has maintained a strong focus on candidates with Canadian work experience and those holding provincial nominations."

— CIC News analysis

What CEC Candidates Need to Know

The Canadian Experience Class is open to workers who have gained at least one year of skilled work experience in Canada within the three years before applying. Unlike the Federal Skilled Worker program, CEC does not require a labour market assessment or job offer, making it a popular pathway for temporary workers and international graduates already in Canada.

With CRS scores holding near 516, candidates typically need a combination of strong language test results, a bachelor's degree or higher, and several years of Canadian work experience to be competitive. Age also plays a significant role — the CRS system awards maximum points to candidates between 20 and 29.

The next CEC draw has not been announced, but IRCC has been holding CEC rounds roughly every two weeks through 2026.
